parsedVerdict.reasoning: StartSubscription is a standard application-layer use case. It validates its input, gets the plan through a domain port, checks that the customer does not already hold an active subscription on the same plan, and has the domain factory (Subscription.start) build the aggregate. It then saves the result through the repository port and maps it to an application DTO. Nothing in it is persistence, transport or framework code: there is no SQL, no HTTP handling and no ORM. The duplicate-plan check reads other stored subscriptions through the repository, so it is reasonable for the use case to do it. The seat check (`!Number.isInteger(seats) || seats < 1`) is the one borderline item. It could be read as a domain invariant that belongs in Subscription.start. However, it works as up-front input validation using a domain error, which is acceptable in a use case, and the source does not show that it repeats or replaces domain logic. ExecuteContextDto only carries an optional requestId, which is ordinary request metadata for the application layer, not transport logic.
